h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר כ״ד Pesach — Maamar Kaf Daled

p: שַׁבָּת חוֹל הַמּוֹעֵד פֶּסַח
Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach
"תְּחִילָּה לְמִקְרָאֵי קֹדֶשׁ זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָיִם, כִּי בָנוּ בָחַרְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר."
"The first of the holy convocations, a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt, for You have chosen us, etc."
וְכֵן בְּלוּחוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת
And likewise in the Second Tablets
(דְּבָרִים ה', ט"ו):
(Devarim 5:15):
וְזָכַרְתָּ כִּי עֶבֶד הָיִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר עַל כֵּן צִוְּךָ ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
"And you shall remember that you were a slave, etc.; therefore Hashem your God commanded you to make the Shabbos day."

וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין: בִּשְׁלָמָא הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה רְגָלִים הֵם זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם—פֶּסַח יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שָׁבוּעוֹת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, סוּכּוֹת עַנְנֵי הַכָּבוֹד—אֲבָל שַׁבָּת בַּמָּה הִיא זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם?!

Now one must understand: it makes sense that the three pilgrimage festivals are a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt—Pesach for the Exodus itself, Shavuos for the Giving of the Torah, and Sukkos for the Clouds of Glory—but in what way is Shabbos a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt?!
וְהָעִנְיָן הוּא: דְּנוֹדָע כִּי בְּצֵאת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶם לְמִצְרַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
The explanation is that it is well known that when the Children of Israel went out of Egypt there was no outward distinction between them and the Egyptians, as they said
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב', ה'):
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:5):
גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי — שֶׁהָיוּ אֵלּוּ עֲרֵלִים וְאֵלּוּ עֲרֵלִים, אֵלּוּ מְגַדְּלֵי בְּלוֹרִית וְכוּלֵּי
"'A nation from the midst of a nation'—for these were uncircumcised and those were uncircumcised, these grew pagan locks of hair and those grew pagan locks of hair, etc."

רַק שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָשַׁק בָּהֶם וְנִשְׁבַּע לְגוֹאֲלָם, וּבְחַסְדּוֹ הַגָּדוֹל הֵאִיר וְהוֹפִיעַ בְּתוֹךְ עוֹמֶק לְבָבָם מִגּוֹדֶל קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ בְּלִי הֲכָנָה מִצִּדָּם עַד שֶׁהוֹצִיאָם מִמִּצְרַיִם.

only that the Holy One, blessed is He, desired them and swore to redeem them, and in His great kindness shone and radiated His immense holiness into the depths of their hearts without any prior preparation on their part, until He brought them out of Egypt.
וְלָכֵן נִצְטַוִּינוּ לִזְכּוֹר בְּכָל יוֹם יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
And therefore we are commanded to remember the Exodus from Egypt every single day,
וְאֵין הַמְכוּוָן עַל הַזְּכָרָה בַּפֶּה בִּלְבַד, אֶלָּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּבָר זֶה נִקְבָּע בְּעוֹמֶק לֵב כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
and the intent is not merely verbal mention, rather that this truth be firmly fixed in the depths of every Jew's heart:
שֶׁבְּאִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יִהְיֶה מְשׁוּקָּע בְּאֵיזֶה תַּאֲוָה וְסִיאוּב רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן וְלֹא יוּכַל לָשׁוּת עֵצָה בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, אַל יִתְיָיאֵשׁ עַצְמוֹ,
that if, God forbid, he finds himself sunken in some lust or defilement—may the Merciful One save us—and can find no counsel within his own soul, he should never despair of himself,
רַק שֶׁיַּאֲמִין וִיצַפֶּה לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיוֹצִיאוֹ מֵהַסְגִּירוֹ,
rather he should believe and hope in Hashem, may He be blessed, Who will release him from his confinement,

כִּי יִתְחַזֵּק לְבָבוֹ שֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ מְשׁוּקָּע יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁהָיוּ אָז יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּקָּעִים בְּאַרְבָּעִים וְתֵשַׁע שַׁעֲרֵי טוּמְאָה, וְה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הוֹצִיאָם מִשָּׁם בְּלִי אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא—כֵּן גַּם לִי יַעֲזוֹר ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ.

strengthening his heart with the realization that he is no more sunken than Israel were then in the forty-nine gates of impurity, yet Hashem, may He be blessed, brought them out from there without any awakening from below—so too will Hashem, may He be blessed, help me!
וְלָזֶה נִצְטַוִּינוּ לִזְכּוֹר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
And for this purpose we were commanded to remember the Exodus from Egypt.
וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן הוּא גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת:
Now this very same principle is also the holiness of Shabbos:
כִּי נֹחַ נִצְטַוָּה: יוֹם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ, וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב מִיתָה
for the descendants of Noach were commanded "day and night they shall not cease," and an idolater who observes a day of complete rest incurs the death penalty
(סַנְהֶדְרִין נ"ח:),
(Sanhedrin 58b),
כִּי אֵין נָאֶה לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לִהְיוֹת לָהֶם מְנוּחָה, כִּי תֵּיכֶף עוֹסְקִים בְּדִבְרֵי טִיפְלוּת וְלֵיצָנוּת
because rest is unbefitting for the nations, as immediately upon resting they engage in frivolity and scoffing
(מְגִילָּה י"ב:),
(Megillah 12b),
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ
and in the Midrash
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ל"ט, ח')
(Bereishis Rabbah 39:8)
כְּשֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם לְסוּלָּמָהּ שֶׁל צוֹר וְרָאָה אוֹתָם נוֹכְשִׁים בִּשְׁעַת נִיכּוּשׁ וְכוּלֵּי, אָמַר: יְהֵא חֶלְקִי בָּאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת שֶׁעוֹסְקִים בְּיִשּׁוּבוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
when Avraham came to the Ladder of Tyre and saw them weeding during the weeding season, etc., he said, "May my portion be in this land where they are occupied with the settlement of the world,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and as they said
(סַנְהֶדְרִין ע"ב.):
(Sanhedrin 72a):
שַׁלְוַת רְשָׁעִים רַע לָהֶם וְרַע לָעוֹלָם
"The tranquility of the wicked is bad for them and bad for the world"
כִּי לֹא לָהֶם יָאוּת הַמְּנוּחָה.
for rest does not befit them.
אֲבָל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהִיפּוּךְ: שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ עַל הַמְּנוּחָה בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, וּבוֹ בַּיּוֹם מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ קְדוּשָּׁה בְּלִי שׁוּם אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא,

With Israel, however, it is the exact opposite: they were commanded to rest on the Shabbos day, and on that very day Hashem, may He be blessed, bestows holiness upon them without any prior awakening from below;
וְאֵינוֹ מִצַּד פְּעוּלַּת הָאָדָם רַק מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבָּחַר בָּנוּ מִכָּל הָעַמִּים וְהִבְדִּילָנוּ מֵהֶם וְנָתַן לָנוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת,
it does not stem from human initiative, rather solely from Hashem, may He be blessed, Who chose us from all the nations, separated us from them, and granted us the holiness of Shabbos
וּבָזֶה הוּא שַׁבָּת זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן בְּלִי שׁוּם אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְכָאָמוּר.
and in this way Shabbos is a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt, which likewise occurred without any awakening from below, as explained.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Night of Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach 2 — “In Mishneh Torah the reason for Shabbos is given from man’s side: ‘And you shall remember that you were a slave… therefore Hashem commanded you to make the Shabbos day.’ That is, a person cannot fix the holiness of Shabbos within himself unless he remembers well that he was a slave in the land of Egypt, that is, remembers well the place he stood, in great forgetfulness. Through this remembering the holiness is fixed in him with greater strength, permanently, so that he will never forget.” Connection: Like this maamar, it explains why Shabbos is a remembrance of the Exodus through recalling one’s own low state, and adds that this recall is what fixes in the heart the holiness that Hashem gives.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Parashas Parah 5647 — “Hashem arranged that purity is attained through trial and refining in this world; therefore Israel were in Egypt in the iron furnace and sank into the forty-nine gates of impurity, until they merited to go out from there and acquire purity, ‘a pure thing from an impure.’ So it is every year: every Shabbos is a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt, for on each and every Shabbos one merits to go out from the gates of impurity to the gates of purity. For purity is a gift from Heaven, and one merits it according to one's toil and trial.” Connection: The Sefas Emes also makes each Shabbos a renewed exodus from the gates of impurity, received as a heavenly gift; he adds that the weekday toil and trial are what make one fit for that gift, where Rav Tzadok stresses that it comes without any awakening from below.
